title: Cleaning and Damage Fees Level Descriptor Sheet
content:
Every Cleaning and Damage Fees assessment is held at one of six fee levels. A level covers the incidents its description, its affected extent, its offline and professional-cleaning assumptions and its odor-treatment flag describe, and only the incident categories its entry gate lists. The typical incidents shown for a level are examples of it, not a closed list.

## Ranking

The six levels rank from lowest to highest as follows; "lower" and "higher" level always refer to this order.

| Rank | Fee level |
|---|---|
| 1 | Cleaning Fee Level 1 (Minor) |
| 2 | Cleaning Fee Level 2 (Moderate) |
| 3 | Cleaning Fee Level 3 (Significant) |
| 4 | Cleaning Fee Level 4 (Major) |
| 5 | Damage Fee (Interior Repair) |
| 6 | Damage Fee (Exterior Repair) |

The first four are the cleaning levels; the last two are the damage levels.

## What each level covers

| Fee level | What the level covers | Affected extent |
|---|---|---|
| Cleaning Fee Level 1 (Minor) | Small spill, crumbs or litter on one spot that the driver can clean with wipes in minutes | A single spot |
| Cleaning Fee Level 2 (Moderate) | Spill, litter, odor or animal mess on one seat or floor area needing a hand clean before the next trip | A single seat or floor area |
| Cleaning Fee Level 3 (Significant) | Mess on up to two seats or a seat and its floor, or any bodily fluid on one surface, needing the vehicle taken offline for cleaning | Up to two surfaces |
| Cleaning Fee Level 4 (Major) | Bodily fluids on several surfaces, seat wells, carpet, headliner or vents, needing professional detailing | Multiple surfaces |
| Damage Fee (Interior Repair) | Interior components broken, torn, burned or stained beyond cleaning and needing repair or replacement | An interior component |
| Damage Fee (Exterior Repair) | Exterior panels, lights, mirrors or glass damaged by the rider and needing repair | An exterior component |

## Level assumptions

| Fee level | Vehicle assumed taken offline | Professional cleaning or detailing required | Odor treatment part of the level |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cleaning Fee Level 1 (Minor) | No | No | No |
| Cleaning Fee Level 2 (Moderate) | No | No | Yes |
| Cleaning Fee Level 3 (Significant) | Yes | No | Yes |
| Cleaning Fee Level 4 (Major) | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Damage Fee (Interior Repair) | Yes | No | No |
| Damage Fee (Exterior Repair) | Yes | No | No |

## Entry gates

A level's entry gate lists the incident categories the level may hold, and every entry gate requires the trip to be completed.

| Fee level | Incident categories its entry gate lists |
|---|---|
| Cleaning Fee Level 1 (Minor) | food or drink spill; trash or debris; animal hair or mess |
| Cleaning Fee Level 2 (Moderate) | food or drink spill; trash or debris; smoke or vape odor; animal hair or mess |
| Cleaning Fee Level 3 (Significant) | food or drink spill; smoke or vape odor; animal hair or mess; bodily fluids |
| Cleaning Fee Level 4 (Major) | bodily fluids |
| Damage Fee (Interior Repair) | interior damage |
| Damage Fee (Exterior Repair) | exterior damage |

Read the other way round, the same gates give, for each incident category the driver reports, the levels whose entry gate lists it:

| Incident category reported | Levels whose entry gate lists it |
|---|---|
| food or drink spill | Levels 1, 2 and 3 |
| trash or debris | Levels 1 and 2 |
| smoke or vape odor | Levels 2 and 3 |
| animal hair or mess | Levels 1, 2 and 3 |
| bodily fluids | Levels 3 and 4 |
| interior damage | Damage Fee (Interior Repair) |
| exterior damage | Damage Fee (Exterior Repair) |

## Typical incidents

| Fee level | Typical incidents |
|---|---|
| Cleaning Fee Level 1 (Minor) | coffee spill on one seat; food wrappers left behind |
| Cleaning Fee Level 2 (Moderate) | soda spilled across a seat; strong vape odor; pet mess on a floor mat |
| Cleaning Fee Level 3 (Significant) | vomit on one seat; large drink spill on seat and floor |
| Cleaning Fee Level 4 (Major) | vomit on several seats and carpet; urine soaked into a seat |
| Damage Fee (Interior Repair) | torn seat upholstery; broken interior door handle; cigarette burn |
| Damage Fee (Exterior Repair) | kicked door panel dent; broken side mirror; cracked window |

## Reading the sheet

- **Does the entry gate of Cleaning Fee Level 4 (Major) list a food or drink spill?** No. Its entry gate lists bodily fluids only, so a spill of food or drink is not a category that level lists.
- **Which cleaning levels list trash or debris?** Cleaning Fee Level 1 (Minor) and Cleaning Fee Level 2 (Moderate); the entry gates of Levels 3 and 4 do not list it.
- **Which levels assume the vehicle was taken offline?** Cleaning Fee Level 3 (Significant), Cleaning Fee Level 4 (Major) and both damage levels.
